code_health.buffers_bounded.note: Bounded: fixed-length reads are clamped, pages are limited to PAGE_LENGTH, and the capacity of the response buffer is handed to the exchange through responseLength. Not bounded: lengths read from the card replace the caller's length with no compare to the destination buffer, the BER limit is a fixed 2048 and runs after a stack array is sized from the same length, and the ATR path has no limit. See the first two defects. Scope: the BER and ATR readers are audited because they take lengths from the card and issue exchanges; CIE file logic and the unfinished crypto code are left out because they do not drive the PN532.

defects.what: readElementaryFile() replaces the caller's *contentLength with a length read from the card and then writes that many bytes into contentBuffer with no compare to the buffer size, so a long file overflows the caller's buffer (the BER path is limited only to about 2048 bytes, the ATR path not at all, and the ReadAll example passes 600).
defects.judged: determineLength overwrites *contentLength with the card's length, nothing compares it to the buffer, and readBinaryContent writes that many bytes; the BER path fails only above 2048 and the ATR path has no limit, while ReadAll allocates 600. It needs a file longer than the caller's buffer, which is not the case the example sizes are written for.

defects.what: readTriples() declares a stack array sized by a length read from the card (up to 65535) and fills it before the BER_READER_MAX_LENGTH check runs, so a card can overflow the stack.
defects.judged: The VLA is sized by a card-supplied 16-bit contentLength and is filled at line 75, while the BER_READER_MAX_LENGTH test comes at line 101. Genuine OIDs are short, so this needs a crafted OID triple.

defects.what: cie_Nfc_Adafruit::begin() enters an endless loop when getFirmwareVersion() returns 0 and returns void, so a missing or dead chip stops the whole program and the caller gets no error.
defects.judged: begin() returns void and spins in while (1) when getFirmwareVersion() returns 0, and cie_PN532::begin() calls it directly, so a dead chip stops the program with no error to the caller. A working chip passes, so this happens only after a fault.

defects.what: readBinaryContent() copies the requested number of bytes out of responseBuffer without comparing them to the returned response length and without checking the preamble octets, so a short response with status 9000 puts uninitialized heap bytes into the caller's buffer.
cie_BerReader::detectLength() ignores the result of readOctets(), so after a failed exchange it builds contentLength from an uninitialized buffer and returns true.

readBinaryContent() ends its page loop on offset < contentLength although offset starts at startingOffset, so a read longer than one page from a nonzero offset can stop early and return true with part of the buffer unfilled (offset 1000, length 300 stops after 228 bytes).
No result of new is checked, so where new returns a null pointer instead of throwing, a failed allocation is used directly, for example as the response buffer of an exchange.
readTriples() ignores the result of readBinaryContent() for an object identifier and then compares the uninitialized array with the known OIDs.
hasSuccessStatusWord() reads response[responseLength-2] with no check that the length is at least 2, so a response of 0 or 1 bytes is read out of bounds.
begin() does not check SAMConfig() and cannot report a failure because it returns void, so a failed SAM configuration looks the same as no card being present.

detectCard() assigns NULL_EF to _currentDedicatedFile instead of _currentElementaryFile, so the cached EF is not cleared there; the effect is masked because ensureDedicatedFileIsSelected() clears it on the next selection.

cie_Nfc has no virtual destructor, so delete _nfc through the base pointer in ~cie_PN532() is undefined behaviour and ~cie_Nfc_Adafruit(), which frees the Adafruit_PN532 object, is not guaranteed to run.
isCardValid() never deletes the cie_Key it allocates, on either return path, so each call leaks the object and its 260 bytes of key data.

readBinaryContent() uses 2 preamble octets for a page of exactly 0x80 bytes, but the BER short form ends at 0x7F (this library's own parser treats 0x80 as indefinite length), so such a page is parsed one octet off.
Two loops that run one exchange per pass have no iteration limit and end only on a read failure or a match, and their word offset wraps, so a card that keeps returning status 9000 keeps them running.
The definition of cie_Nfc_Mock::expectCommand takes byte *response while its declaration takes word *response, so the test sketch does not compile as written.
cie_Nfc_Mock::expectCommands() ignores count and allocates a zero-length array that expectCommand() then writes past, and clear() calls delete [] on arrays that the test holds on its stack.
The getting-started code writes cie_PN532 cie(); which C++ parses as a function declaration, so the cie.begin() that follows does not compile.

code_health.errors_returned.note: Most functions return bool, so failure can be told from success, but not one failure from another: no card, a chip failure and a card status word all give false, and the reason goes only to Serial. begin() returns void and halts.

code_health.buffers_bounded.note: Bounded: the fixed-length files through clamp, each page through PAGE_LENGTH, and the BER content length through BER_READER_MAX_LENGTH. Not bounded: read_EF_DH and read_EF_ATR ignore the caller's capacity, the OID array is sized from the card before any check, and the copy in readBinaryContent ignores the returned length. See defects.

code_health.allocation_checked.searched: All new expressions in cie_*.cpp, and nothrow, == NULL, == nullptr, != NULL, != nullptr: no result of new is compared. The only NULL test in the code is on the callback at cie_BerReader.cpp line 92.

defects.what: read_EF_DH and read_EF_ATR replace *contentLength with the length found on the card and write that many bytes to contentBuffer, so the capacity passed by the caller is ignored and a card file longer than the buffer overruns it (up to about 2 KB for EF_DH, no limit for EF_ATR; cie-ReadAll passes a 600-byte buffer).
defects.judged: readTriples and detectLength replace *contentLength with a value from the card and readElementaryFile reads that many bytes into contentBuffer, so the capacity from the caller is lost. cie-ReadAll passes 600 bytes for both files, and a card file can be longer.

defects.what: readBinaryContent ends its loop on offset < contentLength, which compares an absolute offset with a relative length: with a nonzero starting offset and more than one page the loop stops early and the function returns true with part of the buffer unwritten (offset 100, length 300 reads 228 bytes).
defects.judged: The page size uses contentLength + startingOffset - offset, but the loop ends on offset < contentLength, so start 100 and length 300 read one page of 228 bytes and return true. readKey with start 8 and length 257 happens to pass, yet readBinaryContent is public and many such pairs give a false success.

defects.what: Card layer, above the chip protocol: isCardValid can never return true, because verifyInternalAuthenticateResponse is a stub that returns false, so a genuine card is reported as invalid after the exchanges are made.
defects.judged: verifyInternalAuthenticateResponse is a stub that returns false, so isCardValid() cannot return true and cie-ReadID prints a genuine card as probably a clone. The README warning that clones are not yet detected does not change the behaviour of the public function.

defects.what: With a dead chip, begin() stops the program in an endless loop, and it returns void, so the caller cannot detect the failure or try again.

hasSuccessStatusWord reads response[responseLength-2] with no check of the length, so a successful exchange that returns 0 or 1 bytes reads before the start of the heap buffer and decides on those bytes.

readBinaryContent always copies contentPageLength bytes and ignores the length returned in responseLength, so a shorter response that ends in 90 00 fills the caller's buffer with uninitialized heap bytes and returns true.
defects.judged: The copy loop runs to contentPageLength regardless of the responseLength that sendCommand updates, and hasSuccessStatusWord looks only at the last two returned bytes. A short response ending in 90 00 returns true with the status word and uninitialised heap bytes in the content.

defects.what: readTriples allocates a variable-length stack array with a length taken from the card, before the check against BER_READER_MAX_LENGTH, so a malformed OBJECT IDENTIFIER length can overflow the stack.
defects.judged: The VLA for an OBJECT IDENTIFIER is sized by contentLength from the card at line 74 and the BER_READER_MAX_LENGTH test is at line 101, so the length can reach 65535 before any check.

defects.what: Two card reads in the BER reader ignore the returned bool: after a failed read, detectLength builds the content length from an uninitialized heap buffer and returns true, and readTriples compares an uninitialized OID.
defects.judged: Both calls return bool and the result is dropped, so after a failed read detectLength builds a length from an uninitialised heap buffer and returns true, and readTriples compares an uninitialised stack array. It needs a failed read, such as a lost card.

defects.what: No result of new is checked, and on the AVR core operator new[] returns the NULL from malloc (~/.arduinocdt/packages/arduino/hardware/avr/1.8.2/cores/arduino/new.cpp), so with the heap exhausted the null pointer goes to the exchange and to the copy loops.
defects.judged: No new is checked, and AVR 1.8.2 new.cpp returns malloc directly, so a NULL reaches the exchange and the copy loops. These sizes are about 260 bytes at most, so it needs an exhausted heap rather than a length from a card.

defects.what: cie_AtrReader::detectLength and cie_BerReader::detectTag have no limit of their own: they end only on a match or a read error, so a card that keeps returning 90 00 keeps the program in the loop, and on AVR the 16-bit offset wraps.
defects.judged: Both loops have no count limit and end only on a match or a failed read, and word is 16 bits on AVR, so the offset wraps. A card that ends the file with an error status stops them, and removing the card gives the read error that ends the loop, so the program stays there only while such a card is held in the field.

defects.what: detectCard assigns NULL_EF to _currentDedicatedFile instead of _currentElementaryFile; the old value is cleared later only because ensureDedicatedFileIsSelected clears it when the DF differs.
isCardValid allocates a cie_Key and never deletes it, on the early return and at the end, so each call loses the object and its 260 bytes of key data.

cie_PN532 deletes _nfc through cie_Nfc, which has no virtual destructor, so ~cie_Nfc_Owner does not run and the Owner_PN532 object is not freed; deleting a derived object this way is undefined behaviour.
The getting-started sketch writes cie_PN532 cie(); which declares a function, so the cie.begin() that follows does not compile.
A comment in cie_PN532.h tells I2C users to define the IRQ and reset pins, but PN532_IRQ and PN532_RESET are used nowhere and the library has no I2C path.

The test mock cannot compile and is wrong if it did: expectCommand is declared with word *response and defined with byte *response, printHex receives a byte where it needs a pointer, and expectCommands sets the count to 0 and allocates an empty array that expectCommand then writes to.
